A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AG-REPA work. All 13 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including Appendix A in v1 and Appendices A–C in v2, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 and Tables 1–4 report original layer-probing, alignment, convergence, and audio-generation experiments, including WER, FAD, and MOS results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds architecture comparisons, efficiency measurements, stability analyses, and ablations in Tables 5–12, plus MOS statistical analysis in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The main FoG-A scoring, Top-K selection, weighting, and alignment objective remain unchanged. Appendix B adds experimental adaptations using internal deeper-feature supervision and timestep-dependent routing/projection heads, changing targets or alignment procedures for those variants. Appendix A.4 expands the specification of the already-described adaLN-Zero backbone.

E1.justification: Both versions cover LibriSpeech speech and AudioSet general audio, TTS/TTA, and token configurations A and B. Voicebox, CosyVoice, and F5-TTS were already evaluated in v1. The additional experiments use retained coverage without introducing another dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Shallow REPA only on the unified DiT; v2 Table 5 adds it to comparisons on F5-TTS, Voicebox, and CosyVoice. Table 12 introduces LayerSync-style internal self-alignment comparisons, while Table 11 evaluates convolutional projection alternatives, including an iREPA-style head. These substantially strengthen the comparator set.

E3.justification: Although v1 Table 3 already reports 500k-step results, Appendix A.5 replaces its one-epoch warm-up and two subsequent epochs with a 5,000-step warm-up and fixed 500k checkpoint. New controlled experiments vary layer count, weighting, projection design, supervision, and refresh/routing schedules. These are reported protocol revisions and additions; rerunning retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's layer-selection and architecture experiments, v2 tests diagnostic overhead, ranking stability across checkpoints, freezing versus refreshing, static versus timestep-adaptive routing, layer-count and weighting sensitivity, projection heads, and supervision sources (Tables 6–12). Table 5 additionally tests whether the shallow-layer heuristic transfers across architectures.

E5.justification: Three-seed objective-metric averaging is retained. v2 identifies the existing MOS uncertainty terms as standard errors and adds 95% confidence intervals and paired two-sided tests against REPA at L4,8,12, with p=0.004 for speech and p=0.011 for audio. Appendix C specifies sample-level aggregation; no increased seed count or objective-metric variance reporting is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain their numerical results. Table 3 revises FoG-A's reported selection from L1/L2/L9 to L1/L2/L7 and adds Audio FAD for random, LASP, and gradient-norm selection: 3.32, 3.21, and 2.71. Tables 5–12 add substantial comparison, stability, sensitivity, and efficiency results. These additions do not constitute improved scores for unchanged AG-REPA settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the inference drawn from the retained Jacobian-product equation. v1 asserts amplification and disproportionate early-layer sensitivity; v2 explains that the product may amplify, preserve, or attenuate perturbations and does not prove universal early-layer dominance. This is a limited mathematical-reasoning correction, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central SCD/FoG-A contributions are retained. The introduction narrows the claimed 18%/16% FAD reductions from the best fixed-layer baselines to the best single-fixed-layer baseline, matching Table 2. The conclusion adds tentative extension to other residual generators and qualifies the applicability of static selection.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 replaces blanket descriptions of deep storage and inactive deep layers with teacher- and topology-dependent interpretations consistent with Table 1. v2 also qualifies the sensitivity argument, explains static-selection and projection-head tradeoffs, and introduces specific limitations concerning longer training, representation drift, and teachers retaining dense temporal or spatial structure.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address and substantial implementation disclosures: probing every 200 steps, batches of at most two samples, alternating 12 of 24 layers, rank-0 execution, and training batch size 16. Appendix C specifies VGGish FAD with 16 kHz resampling and blinded MOS evaluation using 20 raters and 40 samples per method. These are newly documented details, not established changes to previously undisclosed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Haghighi et al.'s LayerSync and positions supervision source as complementary to AG-REPA's layer-selection contribution. Section 2.2 also qualifies its characterization of existing audio-alignment approaches. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. v2 makes localized rewrites in related work, mechanistic discussion, and the conclusion; removes several paragraph labels; and adds Section 5.5, appendix subdivisions, code availability, and disclosure text. Author-affiliation and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: Eight new tables, Tables 5–12, substantially expand the results presentation. Table 3 gains an Audio FAD column and expanded convergence footnote, while Table 2 revises its baseline label and caption. All four figure artworks are retained; Figure 1's caption changes, and Figure 4 moves with Appendix A.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in the justification for causal layer selection: Table 5 tests the competitive shallow heuristic across architectures, and Tables 7–12 examine stability and previously unsupported design choices. It also corrects the Jacobian-amplification argument, aligns the SCD interpretation with Table 1, and makes MOS evidence assessable through Appendix C. Epoch-to-step correspondence remains insufficiently explained and objective-metric variance remains unreported, but the gains in evidential support, scientific precision, and reproducibility are substantial.
